review_notes: Source-first scope: the introduction states the principal research issue as whether SFAS 131 improves investors’ and analysts’ ability to predict firm performance. Section 5.2.1 and Table 4 directly test the first analyst-access question: whether analyst earnings and revenue forecasts reflect the new segment information before its public release. Retain its parallel AEF and ARF outcomes, both equation (1) comparisons (SFAS 14 versus SFAS 131 mechanical forecast inputs), and pooled equation (2) interaction fits. Section 5.2.2 calls the post-release forecast-accuracy analysis the next question; the later trading-rule, mechanical-forecast-difference determinants, and monitoring analyses are follow-ups to separate questions, so they are outside this selected family.

Appendix B forecast definitions are supplied in the current independently checked reading derivative and have been expanded here. They are deterministic measurement inputs, not fitted construction regressions, so no supporting regression dependency is needed. Preserve the source’s signed SALEDEV cutoff versus “within 5%” prose, unspecified constant growth rate for segments without an SIC code, literal negative-earnings branches/equality gaps, EARNDEV correction rules, and Table 3 ×100 versus Table 4 dollar-per-share scaling conflict.

The paper identifies these specifications only as regressions; the underlying estimator is not reported. The Table 4 fits have exact per-fit Ns from the coordinator-verified transcription appended to physical reading page 29. Adoption years vary across firms, so no single calendar window is reported.
